drafted_from: tool:make-tracked-link's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a tracked link with UTM fields for a post, ad, email or bio, so visits and sales can be traced to it", with {"destination":"https://shop.example/offer","project":"spring-launch","source":"instagram","campaign":"reel-12"}. It runs tool:make-tracked-link and answers {"link":"https://shop.example/offer?bf_project=spring-launch&utm_source=instagram&utm_campaign=reel-12","fields":{"bf_project":"spring-launch","utm_source":"instagram","utm_campaign":"reel-12"}} With go_base set to the client site's address it also answers the touch row for journey_touches and the short /go/ link.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and answers, and keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Make a tracked link with UTM fields for a post, ad, email or bio, so visits and sales can be traced to it", and give it destination (The web page the link opens); project (Your name for what is being promoted, letters, numbers, dots, dashes or underscores); source (Where the link is posted, like instagram or newsletter); campaign.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:make-tracked-link and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Adds the project, source and campaign (and optionally the medium and a content tag for one post) to a web address as UTM fields, replacing any already there.

4. For a visitor to be followed from the post to a booking, a checkout and a sale, give it go_base too (the client site's address, like https://site.example). The answer then also carries touch and short_link. The tool keeps no row: write touch into the pursuit's journey_touches table yourself (tool:run-sql-in-my-database; read-data/journey-steps.sql makes the table), and post short_link as the link. A visitor who opens short_link is sent on to the destination with the UTM fields and a touch id, and each click is kept as a step.
